title: A scored test set for what Ask and the Photonz skill make, so we can climb it
goal: One command runs a fixed set of requests (drawings, component sheets, redlines) through Ask and through the Photonz skill, photographs each result and scores it for cleanness, typography, alignment and how closely it did what was asked, so every change to the prompt, the skill or the tools can be kept or thrown away on a number instead of a guess.
notes:
The user, 2026-10-20: 'i would like to hill climb the skill. is there a way we can develop an eval that can adjust the quality of output for drawing and component creation?' and on the component sheet: 'this is a complete mess. there is no table, no alignment, no titles, no clean design. The output should always be clean and beautiful and with consistent typography, alignment, and follow the user's requests as closely as possible.'

What the sheet run did (screenshot saved): place_component Badge, Nav Bar, Card, Text Field, Button, then add_text 'Badge', 'Navigation Bar', 'Card Content', 'Enter text here', 'Click me' laid OVER the components at random sizes; no rows, no state columns, no headers. That is what rule scores must catch.

Engines: Ask goes through the app (AskPlanning.swift, qwen3:30b via Ollama). The skill engine is a headless Claude Code session with only plugin/skills/photonz and the MCP server (Scripts/install-mcp.sh), the way the agent-skill audit ran its four scenarios (queue/audits/2026-10-19-agent-skill-transcript.md). The judge is dev tooling, never in the app; it may use a cloud model. App copy never names Claude or Anthropic.

Keep the run bounded (CLAUDE.md: never leave the machine loaded): one case at a time, a time limit per case, the probe quit at the end. This is the measuring stick only; the climbing is the tasks that depend on it (the dog task, the component sheet task).
acceptance: One command (for example Scripts/ask-eval.sh run --engine ask|skill --tag "<what changed>") runs every case on the probe at Next defaults, saves each result's picture and read document, and prints a score per case and a total. A run appends to a score history file, and the command can compare any run with the best so far, case by case

Cases at start, each a request plus the document it starts on: the user's three failures word for word ("draw a picture of a dog"; "create a smiley face icon"; a table of Apple-quality base components showing their states and text, with titles), the twelve drawings of ask-draws-a-dog-you-can-tell-is-a-dog, a component sheet for a website's design system, measurements on the settings screenshot, and a pricing section on brand. Adding a case is one file

Rule scores read from the document, not the picture: text overlapping text or another layer, things meant to line up that do not (distinct left edges and row tops in a grid, gaps between siblings that differ), how many type sizes and weights are used (a sheet with more than four sizes loses points), every asked-for item present and labelled, nothing off the canvas

A judge scores the picture with a fixed written rubric (clean, consistent typography, aligned, looks designed, did what was asked), 1 to 10 each. The judge is a strong model that can see and did not make the result, the same model and rubric every run, three runs and the median. Drawings are also named blind, as the dog task describes

The judge agrees with the user: the three screenshots the user called a mess (queue/audits/2026-10-20-user-ask-dog.png, queue/audits/2026-10-20-user-ask-smiley-icon.png, queue/audits/2026-10-20-user-ask-component-sheet-mess.png) score low, and a clean component sheet made by hand to the mock's look scores high. If the judge cannot tell them apart, the rubric is fixed before anything else uses it

The audit has the first run's scores for both engines as the baseline, a contact sheet of every case, and how long a whole run takes. Anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar (queue/bin/follow-up-bar.md), and written into this task's log if it does not

log.note: manager 2026-10-20: record how long each case takes as well as its score (Ask took 24.5 s median for the screenshot plan on 2026-10-19), so a change that buys quality with a minute of waiting shows up in the comparison and is not kept by accident.

Adversarial review before building: (1) a judge that is the same model family as the skill engine could flatter it; mitigated by a fresh tool-limited session that sees only the picture, never the transcript, and by calibrating on the user's own verdicts first. (2) Blind naming leaks when a drawing writes its own name (the user's dog had 'Dog' over it, and the namer said dog 2 of 3): naming counts 0 when the drawing's words contain the name. (3) Rule scores from frames alone can be gamed by a tidy grid of nonsense; that is why they are only 30-40% of a case and the judge holds the rest. (4) The skill engine is told one sentence about what is open (Ask knows it from the app); recorded in the README. (5) Under a locked screen Ask is found by name, so the ask engine cannot run then; the run stops and says so.

Judge calibration passed on rubric first try: user dog 1.8, user smiley 1.8, user component sheet 1.4 (all 4 or under), clean sheet made by hand through the MCP tools 7.6 (7 or over). Judge: claude-opus-5-5, fresh claude -p session with only Read, no settings, no MCP, 3 looks, median per line.
owns no walks; the ones it names are examples

Follow-ups: none filed. Every rough line is covered: Ask's drawings by ask-draws-a-dog-you-can-tell-is-a-dog, its sheets by asking-for-a-sheet-of-components-gives-a-clean-t and asking-for-base-components-builds-the-real-set-w, pricing and measurement crowding by ask-on-the-local-model-makes-results-that-look-f (baselines and commands folded into each). Left rough here: the judge is the skill engine's own model (a fresh session that sees only the picture; calibration passed but no third maker's picture is in the set yet); a runner must run in --minutes pieces; measurement readouts crowd for the skill too (folded into the local-model task, may be the Measure tool's placement).

Scripts/ask-eval.sh (Scripts/ask-eval/, README there): 17 cases run one at a time on the probe through Ask or the skill, read and rendered over MCP, scored by document rules (14 node tests), a fixed-rubric picture judge (claude-opus-5-5, 3 looks, median) and blind naming; history in queue/evals/ask-eval-history.jsonl with compare against the best, seconds per case. Judge agrees with the user (messes 1.8/1.8/1.4, hand-made clean sheet 7.6). Baselines: Ask 37.8 in 10.5 min, skill 83.9 in 24.5 min. Audit queue/audits/2026-10-20-ask-eval.json with both contact sheets. Scripts/test.sh 14008 green.
